title: The Nobel brain drain: where laureates were born, and where they won
excerpt: I drew a line from birthplace to prize for 760 Nobel prizes in the sciences and economics. 31% went to someone working outside their birth country, the United States gained 131 more laureates than it grew, Germany's share fell from 31% to 7% after 1933, and Japan became a late riser that keeps its laureates.
seo_description: A flow map of Nobel laureates from birthplace to prize: the US as the great importer, Germany after 1933, Japan's rise and the top universities.
header_alt: Title card reading 'The Nobel brain drain' in black and red on cream paper, beside a world map of curved lines from laureates' birthplaces to where they won, most of them red lines from Europe to the United States. Text: where 760 laureates were born and where they did the work that won the prize; 34% of prizes won in the US went to people born abroad.
